claims.text: The Cr/Zr-alloy interface is susceptible to fast diffusion along high-angle grain boundaries.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of unmodified elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
A 20–50 nm TiN interlayer deposited by ALD will act as a robust Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
Pre-deposition surface treatment will enhance adhesion of the TiN-assisted coating system.
ALD will produce a conformal TiN interlayer at the Cr/Zr interface.
The TiN interlayer will be dense and nanocrystalline.
The TiN interlayer will be sufficiently defect-minimized and continuous at the Cr/Zr interface.
The TiN interlayer will remain chemically inert at the Cr/Zr interface.
TiN has a high melting point relevant to its proposed use at accident temperatures.
TiN has sufficiently low diffusivity to impede transport between Cr and Zr.
A continuous TiN layer will physically block atomic interdiffusion paths between Cr and Zr.
The TiN barrier will mitigate diffusion-driven coating failure during transient high-temperature exposure.
The TiN-assisted coating will show lower Cr–Zr interdiffusion depth than an unmodified Cr-coated control.
The TiN-assisted coating will retain better interfacial integrity than an unmodified Cr-coated control.
The TiN-assisted coating will preserve protection during continuous subcritical-water exposure at approximately 350 °C.
The TiN-assisted coating will preserve protection during steam exposure at 1150–1200 °C for 30–60 minutes.
The long-term stability of the TiN barrier under cyclic thermal loading is uncertain.
Pinhole defects may form in the TiN barrier and compromise its performance.
